english.title: Stun poultry by gas exposure on premises other than slaughterhouse for insufficient time or when notice not given
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) at premises, other than a slaughterhouse, used for the killing of animals, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..),

(A)_[stunned]_
(B)_[caused **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to stun]_
(C)_[permitted **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to stun]_

poultry by exposure to gas when

(D)_[each bird was not exposed to the gas for long enough to ensure it was killed]_
(E)_[stunning took place in the knacker's yard where the poultry had been kept for the production of meat, eggs or other products and the owner of the poultry had not given prior written notice to the competent authority, not less than five working days before the date on which the stunning took place]_
(F)_[stunning took place on the farm where the poultry had been kept for the production of meat, eggs or other products and the owner of the poultry had not given prior written notice to the competent authority, not less than five working days before the date on which the stunning took place]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 30(1)(d) and 33(1) of, and paragraph 41(1) of Schedule 2 to, the Welfare of Animals at the Time of Killing (England) Regulations 2015.

other.penalty:
Summary: Fine

Time limit for prosecutions
6 monthsNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
